title: Logical Spectroscopy: Lifted-Product Codes with Addressable Bases
abstract: Quantum LDPC memories can encode many logical qubits, but dimension alone does not make them usable: applications need explicit conjugate logical operators with structured labels and physical representatives. For hypergraph-product (HGP) codes this structure is transparent, since the input matrices are binary and can be row-reduced over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Abelian lifted-product codes are subtler. Their seed entries are shifts, or sparse sums of shifts, in a group-algebra ring rather than a field, so pivot blocks need not be invertible and global row reduction can fail.   We address this with \emph{logical spectroscopy}, a spectral construction that replaces global row reduction by finite-field computations in the Frobenius character packets of the Abelian lift group. The Chinese remainder theorem (CRT) decomposes the group algebra into these packets. In each packet, we compute kernels, quotients, and product-complex homology; we then lift the resulting representatives back with CRT idempotents and pair $X$ and $Z$ logicals through reciprocal trace-dual packets. This gives complete addressable conjugate logical bases for finite Abelian lifted products $\mathsf{LP}(A,B)$.   The same packet data also gives design diagnostics. Packet ranks show how logical sectors split, the lifted representatives give certified upper bounds on the width of the constructed conjugate basis, and whole-orbit erasures decompose into packet-attributed erased-logical dimensions. Thus, CRT packets also serve as working coordinates: they label logical sectors, certify the constructed basis width, and attribute structured erasure failures. Under bounded seed-shape and group-basis-support assumptions, this construction gives Abelian lifted-product qLDPC families an HGP-like feature while preserving the layout freedom of group-algebra lifts.
summary: The paper introduces 'logical spectroscopy' as a novel technique to systematically construct and label usable conjugate logical bases for complex lifted-product qLDPC codes. By leveraging the Chinese Remainder Theorem, it replaces failing global algebraic reductions with independent finite-field computations across spectral packets. This provides crucial structural diagnostics necessary for building reliable quantum memory systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a systematic method to construct and label explicit, addressable conjugate logical operators (X/Z pairs) for high-rate Abelian lifted-product quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes.
main_result: The authors introduce 'logical spectroscopy,' a spectral construction that replaces problematic global row reduction with finite-field computations via the Chinese Remainder Theorem, yielding a complete addressable conjugate logical basis.
method: The method decomposes the group algebra using the CRT into spectral packets. Linear algebra is then performed independently within each packet to compute kernels and quotients, which are subsequently lifted back to define structured logical operators.
model_or_system: The work focuses on quantum error-correcting codes, specifically quasi-cyclic qLDPC codes based on lifted-product (LP) constructions over group algebras $R = \mathbb{F}_2[x]/(x^l+1)$.
key_observables: Complete addressable conjugate logical basis; packet ranks showing sector splitting; certified upper bounds on basis width; and packet-attributed dimensions for erasure failures.
important_parameters: The construction is most robust when the lift group order is odd, allowing clean CRT decomposition into finite fields.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on assumptions of bounded seed-shape and bounded group-basis-support. For the spectral method to apply cleanly, the lift group order must be odd.

paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first identifying the failure point (global row reduction over non-fields) and then proposing logical spectroscopy. This involves detailing the CRT decomposition, performing packet-wise linear algebra, pairing X/Z operators via reciprocal trace-duals, and finally presenting diagnostic tools derived from these packets.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful algebraic framework for analyzing structured quantum codes, offering systematic diagnostics that go beyond simple dimension counting to certify the usability of logical qubits in fault-tolerant architectures.

Figure 2 and the tabulated data in Appendix F illus- trate why basis width, distance upper-bound diagnos- tics, and structured-erasure exposure are distinct objec- tives. In the displayed comparison, M45 4,10 has a mod- est certificate and a lower two-left-orbit failure rate than the 3 × 7 monomial benchmarks. The sparse parity- systematic probes P75 3,7 and P91 3,7 repair parts of the trivial- packet rank profile, but they are more exposed to this particular one- and two-left-orbit erasure model. Con- versely, an attractive erasure score does not compensate for a verified small distance upper-bound witness; such seeds should be treated as warning examples rather than benchmark candidates.
